title: Mastra CC protocol
description: The wire contract between the daemon and its one client. Elements are named at the level of meaning: no platform or toolkit identifier appears in any field name, enum value, method name, or description. The single exemption is the diagnostic field.

semanticElement.description: One element, named for what a person means by it.

id.description: Stable identity: a kind prefix and twelve hex digits. Never reused.

role.description: The neutral role vocabulary. A native role with no neutral equivalent maps to generic and keeps its native name in the diagnostic field.

name.description: The human-facing name. Comparisons normalise to NFKC first.

states.description: The states currently true of the element.

actions.description: What a later call could be asked to do. M1 implements none of them.

diagnostic.description: Debug-only carrier and the only exemption from the neutral-vocabulary rule: native identifiers may appear here for a human reading a log, and are never load-bearing.
Native details preserved for a human debugging. Exempt from the neutral-vocabulary rule; never load-bearing for agent logic.

nativeRole.description: The backend's own role word, verbatim.

nativeId.description: The backend's own identifier for the element, verbatim.

queryElements.description: Find elements matching a semantic query. Observation only.

role.description: Restrict the answer to one role.

name.description: Restrict the answer to elements whose normalised name matches.

limit.description: Upper bound on the number of returned elements.

elements.description: Every element that matched, in reading order.

attestElement.description: State what a later call would act on, without acting. Returns the element as currently resolvable, or an explicit refusal naming why.

element.description: Present when the id still resolves.

refusal.description: Present when it does not; names the reason.

openApplication.description: Open an application by name, with its readability applied at the moment it starts. The first effect-class method: visible to the person, trivially reversible. Authority is checked before anything else, and a refusal never reveals whether an application exists on this machine.

name.description: The human-facing application name. Neutral vocabulary; no platform identifiers. Comparisons normalise to NFKC first.

application.description: Present when the application was opened (or was already ours) and became readable.

refusal.description: Present otherwise; names the reason without revealing what is available to other sessions.
